walkthroughs.body_html:
The electromagnetic spectrum is a family of transverse waves.

From longest wavelength to shortest: Radio, Microwaves, Infrared, Visible, Ultraviolet, X-rays, Gamma rays.

Memorise the order — a silly mnemonic helps: "Raging Martians Invaded Venus Using X-ray Guns". 🛸

Here's the wild part: in a vacuum every EM wave travels at the same speed — about 3 × 10⁸ m/s. That's the speed of light, c.

What makes them different is their wavelength and frequency. Long wavelength means low frequency (radio); short wavelength means high frequency (gamma).

Radio: TV and radio broadcasting. Microwaves: heating food, satellite phones. Infrared: TV remotes, thermal cameras, electric heaters.

Visible: vision, fibre-optic cables. Ultraviolet: tanning lamps, security marks, vitamin D. X-rays: medical imaging of bones. Gamma: sterilising equipment, treating cancer.

options: Microwaves
Infrared

mcqs.q: If one EM wave has a higher frequency than another, what is true about its wavelength?
options: It is also longer, because both increase together.
It is unchanged — only the speed differs.
Infrared cameras detect heat moving through the air around objects.
It is shorter — wavelength and frequency are inversely related (c = f x lambda).

mcqs.q: Why are infrared cameras used to detect warm objects in the dark?
options: Infrared cameras shine infrared light onto objects so they reflect back visibly.
Yes — UV is the colour purple.
Infrared cameras detect heat moving through the air around objects.
Warm objects emit infrared radiation due to their temperature; the camera detects this emission.

mcqs.q: Is ultraviolet light visible to humans?
options: No — even though it sits next to violet on the spectrum, its frequency is above the range our eyes detect.
Yes — UV is visible because it's right next to violet.
Yes — UV is the colour purple.
Infrared cameras detect heat moving through the air around objects.
